constraints.evidence: Slide 19 puts the base case at 2.68% ($37.8M) against the 3.0% target. It states the gap as 'About $4.5M short of 3.0%' and sizes a closing lever (3.3 pp of further promotion cuts). Slide 18 nets the $7.1M of known cost increases before reaching $37.8M.

Slide 20 phases FY2026: $15.3M + $5.1M promotions (three quarters) + $1.9M fee (three quarters) − $0.2M delivery rate rise = $22.02M against the $20M covenant. Exits and the labor cut are kept out of FY2026, and a 26.0% promotional-share gate is set as the level that still meets the covenant. No FY2026 downside case is built.

Slides 14 and 16 count the $7.5M exit cost against the $25M cap. Slide 15 notes that private-label development cost is unsized and 'falls under the $25M cap'. The one-time cost of the other moves is not totalled.
Slide 14: six leases lapse by 2027 with no vote. The three early exits need a board vote and cost $7.5M. The vote is placed on the Slide 20 timeline and in the next steps.

The owners' wish to keep delivery is never mentioned. The plan does keep delivery, through the fee rollout, but the commitment is not cited as a constraint and the exit-delivery option is never discussed.
Slide 10 deducts the $7.3M wage rise. Slide 18 deducts $7.1M (a $6.8M wage rise on FY2028 labor plus the $0.3M provider rise) before reaching the $37.8M headline.

Slide 7 gives net e-commerce contribution of −$10.4M: 30% new sales × 20% contribution, less $18.1M fulfillment. It explicitly rebuts the team's 6.1% claim and says a freeze 'does not end' the loss. The 3% provider rise ($0.3M) is carried in Slides 10 and 18.

Slide 10 nets the $14.5M saving against $6.5M of extra shrink to about $8.0M, and shows FY2028 profit of $15.7M. Slide 18 uses $14.2M less $6.1M of shrink = $8.1M. Customer-response sales loss is flagged as not counted.
Slide 12 nets 25% lost volume at 6 cents against the 14 pp gain, giving $6.4M. Depth is kept in the 11 ValuMart trade areas. Vendor funding recovery is explicitly 'not counted'.

Slide 14 builds the $6.6M net figure ($3.1M + $118M × 25% × 12%). The timing (six leases lapse by 2027) and the $7.5M exit cost for three stores are shown. Slide 20 leaves exits out of the FY2026 covenant bridge.

alternatives.evidence: Management's 8% cut is sized net of shrink and the wage rise (Slide 10: $15.7M in FY2028, 1.0% margin) and rejected as the first move. A targeted, sequenced version is adopted: shrink controls first, a shrink gate, hours taken from the most-staffed stores, and the cut placed last. No store-level pilot is described.

The fee rollout is sized ($2.5M, break-even about 12%, Slide 13) and adopted, and the contract renewal is mentioned. Exiting home delivery while keeping click-and-collect is never named or sized, so the board does not see the two options side by side. 'Freeze e-commerce' is the only other option discussed.

Slide 12 sizes the rollback to 24% ($6.4M) against loss-making events (about 11 pp of sales, from the 38% finding). It protects ValuMart areas, which covers the hold-depth option. The second wave to about 21% is sized on Slide 19. The category team's claim is rebutted on Slide 6.

Slide 14 sizes closing all nine ($6.6M). It splits the gain into $4.4M for the six lapsing leases and $2.2M for the three long-lease stores, with a 3.4-year payback on $7.5M. Keeping the three is shown as costing $2.2M a year. The even split is flagged as an assumption.

sensitivities.evidence: Only one shrink response is used (FY2023–25 elasticity, 65% of shrink). Slide 10 shows $6.5M of extra shrink and Slide 18 shows $6.1M. The document gives no shrink increase at which the saving is wiped out or at which the covenant breaks. Customer response and sales loss are flagged as uncounted, and shrink gates at 2.4% and 2.6% are set.

Slide 13 gives a fee break-even: the fee pays while online sales fall less than about 12%, and this is wired into a gate. The cannibalisation rate is never varied from 70%, and no exit-delivery value is shown, so this is only half covered.

The document gives $1.3M per point of promotional share and a stress case with promotions at 26.2% (−0.6 pp margin). The 25% lost-volume share is flagged as an assumption with no lift data. No break-even sales loss at which the saving is erased is shown. The comparable-sales gate at −4.2% is a monitor, not a sensitivity.

overclaim.quote: that clears the covenant and reaches 2.7% by FY2028, and 3.0% with a second promotion wave

omissions: The FY2026 covenant has about $2M of headroom ($22.02M vs $20M). It assumes the full 5 pp promotion reset and the fee effect from Q2. No downside case is run for FY2026: the stress case covers only FY2028, and the fee result is extrapolated from a 4-store, 10-week test. At the 26.0% gate, headroom is only about $0.04M.

The FY2028 figures are labelled 'run-rate'. Exits happen at lease expiry by end-2027, private label ramps over three years, and the labor step starts only after the FY2027 H2 shrink gate. So actual FY2028 operating income and margin, the board's target metric, would fall below the stated $37.8M and 2.7%. No year-by-year path is given.

The path to 3.0% needs 3.3 pp more promotion cut (8.3 of about 11 pp of loss-making volume). It uses a linear $1.3M per point and the same 25% lost-volume rate, with no check on whether the cuts reach areas near ValuMart. The stress case stops at 2.1%.

The one-time costs of other moves are not sized against the $25M cap. These include private-label development and packaging, restoring receiving and rotation hours, and notice costs on the six lapsing leases. The staffing cost of restoring hours in Q1 and Q2 stores is not netted from the $2.3M shrink gain, and this sits against an 8% hours cut elsewhere.
Exiting home delivery while keeping click-and-collect is not sized or argued against the owners' commitment, so the board lacks the full range of delivery options.
unsupported_assumptions: "The lost-volume share is our assumption: the pack has no lift data" (25% of removed promo sales lost at 6 cents). This carries the $6.4M promotions figure and the 3.3 pp second-wave sizing.

"added FY2026–28: 0.75 pp a year, the FY2023–25 pace" gives $3.8M of private-label gain. It assumes the trend continues while promotions are cut and at the full 12 pp premium, and development cost is excluded.
"Losses and sales spread evenly across the nine" gives the $4.4M / $2.2M split and the 3.4-year payback. The pack has no per-store split.
"$2.3M expected gain from shrink controls" assumes equal sales per quartile, recovery of 65% of the quartile gap, and no cost for the restored hours.
Promotions and the fee reset 'from Q2' at full run-rate, giving $5.1M and $1.9M in FY2026. The fee effect is extrapolated from 4 stores over 10 weeks.
